transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
Investigators in Israel believe that the co-pilot who attacked the captain of a plane flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv mid-air last week likely acted alone.
That's according to a person familiar with the matter but not authorized to speak publicly.
NPR's Kat Lonstorf has more from Tel Aviv.
The Israeli investigation into the attack is pointing toward the likelihood that the co-pilot was a lone wolf attacker, that source told NPR.
Investigators in the United Arab Emirates, which is leading the inquiry working with Israeli officials,
announced they have deemed the incident an attempted terrorist attack, although the motive is still unknown.
The co-pilot is from Oman, according to Israeli officials, raising questions about how he was allowed to fly a plane heading to Israel,
as Israel does not allow pilots from countries it doesn't have diplomatic relations with to fly in its airspace.
Several lawmakers in Israel are demanding an investigation into security failures that could have led to the incident.
Kat Lonstorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
The Coast Guard is still searching off the coast of Nantucket for six people missing on a medical transport plane after officials found a debris field from that plane.
Yesterday, the Federal Aviation Administration told the Coast Guard they had lost contact with the Gulfstream G-100 as it traveled from Bermuda to Boston.
Coast Guard Rear Admiral Matt Lake.
We're in the process of working with Massachusetts authorities to get some craft out there that are equipped with sonar to be able to do some detection on the seabed floor.
Six people, including four crew, were on board. The cause of the crash is under investigation.
The Trump administration is giving the public more time to comment on its proposal for unprecedented changes to the next U.S. census.
The plan would reshape the drawing of voting maps and the distribution of federal funding across the country, as NPR's Hansi Lo Wang reports.
Public comments will now be accepted through November 2nd.
The proposal calls for excluding millions of U.S. residents from a census tally that, according to the 14th Amendment, must include the "whole number of persons" in each state.
That count is used to determine each state's share of congressional seats and electoral college votes for a decade.
The Trump administration argues the Constitution's framers did not intend for the word "persons" to include people living in the states without U.S. citizenship or a green card.
Trump officials also propose cutting questions about race and ethnicity because they see a "reduced need" for that information, which is used for civil rights enforcement.
If the proposal is finalized, it's expected to spark lawsuits, and Congress or a new presidential administration in 2029 could reverse any census changes that Trump officials make.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
President Trump is tapping his director of national intelligence, Jay Clayton, to head a new government task force on A.I. that Trump is calling Super Intelligence Task Force.
This after Trump tried to rebrand A.I. as Super Intelligence. It also comes after Trump hosted top A.I. executives at the White House last week.
You're listening to NPR News.
Borders in Brazil are heading to the polls today to choose a new president.
Incumbent Luis Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro, the challenger, are battling for the job.
A runoff will be held later this month if neither candidate gets 50% of the vote.
Lula is a critic of Washington and a supporter of China, and Bolsonaro is the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.
Many churches this weekend are holding their annual "Blessing of the Animals."
Imperes Jason DeRose reports it's an opportunity for people of faith to bring along their pets to worship.
In recent decades, congregations have welcomed pets not just into the parking lot for the annual blessing, but into the pews themselves.
Like at this Episcopal Church in Ventura, California.
Almighty Father, we bless these animals for all they have done for us.
The blessing usually takes place on or near the feast of St. Francis of Assisi, the patron saint of animals and the environment.
Among the stories told about Francis is one in which he preached to birds, telling them they too were loved by God.
The blessing of the animals comes at the end of the new ecumenical season of creation that many churches are marking for the first time this year.
Jason DeRose, NPR News.
It'll be a light week on Wall Street for economic data, as investors focus mostly on the bond market.
They continue to signal big concerns about the global economy.
This says the U.S.-Iran war continues keeping energy costs high when inflation is also high.
You're listening to NPR News.

topics.text: Israeli investigators believe co-pilot who attacked captain on Dubai-Tel Aviv flight acted alone
Coast Guard searches off Nantucket for six people missing on medical transport plane
Trump administration extends deadline for public comments on proposed census changes through November 2nd
Trump appoints Jay Clayton to head new government Super Intelligence Task Force on AI
Brazil's voters head to polls today to choose between incumbent Lula and challenger Bolsonaro
Many churches holding annual Blessing of the Animals this weekend with pets in pews
Wall Street faces light week of economic data with investors focused on bond market concerns
